title: IP Address Splits
statement:
List every valid dotted IPv4 address that can be made by cutting a digit string into four pieces.

Contract
- `digits` is non-null and contains only decimal digits. Lengths outside 4 through 12 have no valid split.
- Return every address formed by four parts in their original order. Each part must be between `0` and `255`, inclusive.
- A multi-digit part may not start with `0`; the single part `0` is allowed.
- Return addresses in lexicographic cut order: try shorter earlier parts before longer earlier parts. Do not mutate the input.

Examples
- `splitIpAddresses("25525511135")` returns `["255.255.11.135", "255.255.111.35"]`.
- `splitIpAddresses("0000")` returns `["0.0.0.0"]`.
- `splitIpAddresses("123")` returns `[]`.
hints: There are only four parts, and each part has length one, two, or three, so enumerate the cut lengths first.
Reject a part as soon as it has a leading zero or a value above 255.
Depth-first search over four parts keeps the ordering simple. Intended complexity is O(1) time and O(1) extra space because a legal IPv4 input has bounded length.
inputSyntax: Input: one digit string, for example: 25525511135
